lines: Mind the toadstools by my door, dearie. The red ones bite back.
I read your tea leaves before you knocked. You will want a stronger brew.
A crow sat on my roof three mornings running. Someone in this city will not see winter.
Feverfew for the head, rue for the heart, and nightshade for whoever wronged you.
Do not thank me for the charm. Thanks binds a debt, and debts get collected.
The mist came thicker last night. It smells of graves and old iron.
Bring me a spider's eye from below and I will brew you something to see in the dark.
They call me a witch to my face and a healer behind closed doors.
Spit thrice over your shoulder before you go down. The deep keeps count of the careless.
Your shadow lags behind you, girl. That is either a blessing or a warning.
I cursed a miller once. His bread still rises crooked, and he still pays me.
Hemlock and honey look alike in a dark jar. Always ask what you are drinking.
The moon is wrong tonight. Keep salt in your boots and your blade close.
Every bone in a troll's hand is good for one wish. Bring me a few.
Wolfsbane grows where the dead are restless. My garden has never been so green.
Hush now, the kettle is listening. It gossips with the chimney.
I see a door in your future, and something hungry waiting behind it.
Pretty boots. Pity about the blood that will be on them by morning.
The priests burn my kind in summer and beg for my poultices in winter.
Dried bat wing, two coppers. Fresh, ten. You do not want to know why.
Never step over a sleeping cat. It steals a year from you each time.
Leave a coin on the hearthstone when you go. My house spirits sulk otherwise.
That ring on your finger hums a sour note. Wear it on the left hand.
Owls hooted my name twice last night. I hooted back, so we are even.
Black candle for banishing, white for mending. Grey ones I keep for myself.
Rub this salve on a wound and it closes. Rub it on a lie and it festers.
The orcs fear nothing but fire and old women who know their true names.
My grandmother warned of the mist before anyone had seen it. Nobody listened to her either.
Plant mandrake by moonlight and stop your ears. Its scream is no lullaby.
You smell of daemon smoke. Wash in running water before you sleep, or it follows you.
Want your fortune? Cross my palm with silver and your heart with courage.
A cracked mirror shows true faces. I keep mine by the door for visitors.
Some nights I hear the dungeon breathing, slow and patient, like something waiting to wake.
Go on, then. Fortune favours the bold and buries the foolish.
I counted all the stars last night. There were eleven, and one was a moth.
If you hold your breath long enough, the mist cannot find you. I am practising.
What has teeth but never eats? My grandfather's comb. And also my grandfather.
I am the king of this puddle. You may kneel, but your knees will get wet.
The chickens told me a secret. I promised not to tell, but it was about eggs.
Why does the sun go away at night? I think it is frightened of the moon.
I wore my boots on the wrong feet so the monsters would follow me backwards.
Riddle me this. What swallows heroes, never chews, and still grumbles? The deep below us.
My hat is full of soup. I keep it there so it stays warm.
A wise man told me to think before I speak. I have been thinking for six years.
Do you want to see my rock? It is very brave. It went down a well once.
Shh! I am hiding from tomorrow. If it cannot find me, it cannot happen.
Spiders have eight legs and no shoes. That is why they are always so angry.
I asked the well what it wanted, and it said water. Then I fell in.
Everybody laughs at the fool, but nobody ever robs the fool. Think about it.
If a troll eats a goat, is it a goat-troll or a troll-goat? Nobody will tell me.
I juggled three apples yesterday. Today I have two apples and a bruise.
The guards say I am harmless. I bit one of them once, just to keep them guessing.
My shadow and I had a fight. It went off sulking under the bridge.
Bones are just skeletons that have stopped trying. Do not stop trying, lady.
Ha! You have a sword! I have a spoon. Mine is better for porridge.
Up is down if you stand on your head long enough. I tried it all morning.
The bell ringer rings the bell. Who rings the bell ringer? I would like to know.
I found a crown in the gutter. It was a turnip, but I wore it proudly.
When the dead walk, I shall walk with them. They seem to know where they are going.
Dogs bark at the moon because it owes them money. Everyone knows that.
A mouse ran up the clock and it never came down. Now it tells the time.
I sing to the cabbages so they grow fat. The cabbages hate my singing.
What is heavier, a pound of feathers or a pound of sorrow? Sorrow. Always sorrow.
You look lost. So am I! Let us be lost together, it is less lonely.
My left foot knows a song my right foot has never heard. They argue at night.
The rich man said I have nothing. Then why does he fear losing what he has?
If you meet an orc, ask it about its mother. It will cry, I promise.
Goodbye! Or hello. I always mix them up, so I say both to be safe.
Repent! The mist is the breath of the saints' anger, and it grows thicker every dawn.
Beneath our feet lies a pit dug by our own sins. Each tier is a vice made flesh.
You carry a sword, sister, but can it cut away the rot within your soul?
The dead rise because the living forgot them. Pray for your ancestors before they come asking.
Gold is the devil's own coin. Spend it on bread and candles, not on wine.
I have seen the end of days in a dream. It smelled of sulphur and burnt bread.
Every daemon in the deep was once a wish someone should never have made.
Kneel now, or kneel later in chains. The choice is yours, but the knee bends either way.
Lust, greed, sloth! I name them, and they shrink. Name your own sins, child.
The mist will swallow the proud first. Their tall towers make easy beacons.
Mark me well. The gate below was opened by mortal hands, and only penance will shut it.
Do you hear the bells? They toll for every soul the dungeon claims.
The faithful need no lantern. The light of the saints walks before them.
Fast and pray, for the hungry spirit sees what the full belly cannot.
Tavern songs today, funeral dirges tomorrow. Turn back while the road is still lit.
Brother against brother, the old prophecy said. Then came the mist, and the prophecy smiled.
Even the spider weaves with patience. Can you not pray with half as much?
Judgement does not knock. It seeps under the door like fog.
Strike down the wicked below, sister, but do not forget the wicked in the mirror.
I was a sinner once, a thief and a liar. Now I am merely a liar who prays.
Your armour is fine work. Pray it holds, for the saints do not mend steel.
Woe to the city that laughs while the abyss yawns beneath its cellars!
The trolls are slow and the undead are slower. Only sin runs faster than you.
Give a coin to the beggar, and the saints give you a feather for your wings.
Open your ears! The stones themselves cry out against our wickedness.
When the last candle gutters, will you be found praying or drinking?
Fire cleanses, water cleanses, but only true sorrow cleanses the heart.
The orc and the daemon are punishments, not accidents. Ask yourself what you did to earn them.
Shut your purse to the moneylender and open your heart to the saints.
They mock me in the square, and the mist creeps closer while they laugh.
Blessed are those who descend into darkness and return carrying the light.
I have preached on this corner nine years. The sinners change, but the sins never do.
Pray before you sleep, pray when you wake, and pray twice before you go below.
Go with the light, sister. And if the light will not go with you, go quickly.
He used to bring me wildflowers from the north road. Now I bring them to him.
The gravedigger says the soil here never settles. I think the dead are still turning over.
Forgive me, I come every morning. Talking to the stone is easier than talking to the living.
My son went down through the gate with a borrowed sword. They never found the sword either.
She hummed while she cooked. I have not been able to cook since she died.
Some nights I hear scratching from below the graves. I tell myself it is only rats.
Plant a rose for the dead and they rest sweeter. That is what my mother told me.
Do not walk on the fresh mounds, please. Some of us are still saying goodbye.
He was a stonemason. Carved half the headstones here, and now someone else carved his.
Grief is a heavy cloak. You stop noticing the weight, but you never take it off.
My sister was so afraid of the dark. I leave a candle burning for her every night.
They say the restless dead below wear the faces of loved ones. I pray I never see his.
I keep his letters under my pillow. The ink is fading faster than my memory.
If you find a silver locket down there, with a crow on its lid, bring it home to me.
The priest promised peace. The priest did not have to bury three children in one winter.
The wind among the stones sounds like whispering. I listen for her voice in it.
We were to be married at harvest. I wore the dress to his burial instead.
Old Tomas laughed louder than anyone in the tavern. The quiet here would have bored him.
Bury them deep, the elders say, or the mist will call them back up.
Every name on these stones was somebody's whole world. Now they are moss and memory.
I lost my husband to the trolls and my faith to the priests. I still have my spite.
Tread softly, adventurer. The graves here are close together, and the dead are easily woken.
My father always said he would die in his bed. The spiders had other plans.
I dream he is knocking at the door. I wake before I learn whether to open it.
Mourning is love with nowhere left to go. So I bring it here.
The ravens know every funeral before the bells ring. I hate those birds.
I visit my grandmother's grave and gossip like she is still alive. She would want the news.
Coming back alive is the only gift you can give those who love you. Remember that below.
A body went missing from this grave last month. The earth was broken from underneath.
I carved her name myself. My hands shook, so the letters lean like she did when tired.
Lay a stone on a grave as you pass. It tells the dead they have not been forgotten.
We buried him without his left hand. Whatever took it is still down there.
Some come to weep, some come to remember. I come because I do not know where else to go.
Go on, live loudly. The quiet comes for all of us soon enough.
Peace be upon you, sister. Silence is the first prayer, and the last.
I have kept my vow of quiet for a year. You are the first I have spoken to today.
Scripture says the lamp is not lit for itself. Shine for others below, and you will not lose your way.
Anger is a hot coal held to throw at another. It burns the hand that holds it.
Our order copies the old books by candlelight. Every word is a small defence against the dark.
Rest awhile if you are weary. Even a blade must return to its sheath.
The undead have no peace to give, so they take ours. Guard your heart before your throat.
Brother Aldric prays in the bell tower at dawn. You may join him, if you can climb.
Bread, water, and a quiet mind. Wealth beyond the reach of any thief.
It is written: fear walks ahead, courage follows behind. Choose who leads.
The mist hides the road, but not the stars. Look up when you are lost.
I tend the herb garden of the cloister. Chamomile for sleep, sage for clear thought.
Do not grieve the monsters you slay, but do not rejoice in their deaths either.
We chant the hours, day and night. Some say our voices keep the deep from waking.
Humility is no weakness. The bowed reed survives the storm that breaks the oak.
A traveller once asked me the way to paradise. I handed him a broom.
Fasting clears the eyes. I have seen more truth on an empty stomach than at any feast.
Forgive yourself for what you could not save. The saints carry the rest.
The relics in our crypt are watched day and night. Some evil wants them very badly.
Each bead on my string is a name I pray for. There is room for yours, if you wish.
The abbot says the dungeon tests the soul as fire tests iron. I pray you ring true.
Speak softly near the chapel. The sisters are at vespers.
Patience, child. The river cuts the mountain not by strength, but by persistence.
We took vows of poverty, yet the poor still come to our gate. We share what little we have.
When the daemon whispers, answer with scripture. It cannot abide the holy words.
My hands were a soldier's once. Now they ring bells and bind wounds instead.
The night office is long and cold. I keep warm by remembering why I sing it.
Blessed water, a little salt, a clean cloth. That is all most wounds truly need.
Do not envy the saints their halos. They earned them in places darker than any dungeon.
Ask your question plainly, sister. Long years of silence have taught me to value few words.
I have prayed over a thousand graves and never once heard the dead complain of the prayers.
The sun rises over the cloister each morning without fail. So shall hope, if you let it.
Kindness costs nothing and buys everything. Spend it freely in this hard world.
Go gently. I shall light a candle for your return.
Three hundred leagues on foot, and my blisters have blisters. The saints had better be listening.
I carry a splinter of the blessed staff in this pouch. It warms my hand at night.
We walk to the cathedral of the white bones. Join us if your road bends that way.
I vowed to walk barefoot to the shrine. I did not vow to stop complaining.
On the road we saw a blind man see again at a wayside chapel. I wept like a child.
My village sent me with their prayers sewn into my cloak. It grows heavier each mile.
Bandits robbed us near the old ruins, then begged our blessing before they fled. Strange times.
Relic sellers everywhere swear their bones are holy. I have bought three thumbs of the same saint.
We sing as we walk, to keep the wolves away. It works on the wolves, less on the innkeepers.
I sleep under hedges and eat what charity allows. I have never felt so rich.
My knees ache from kneeling at every shrine. Each one says it is the holiest.
When I reach the holy site, I shall ask the saint to forgive my brother. He will not ask himself.
The road teaches what sermons cannot. Mostly about mud, and patience.
Do you know a cheap bed in this city? Holy work does not pay well.
I made a vow of silence for the journey. I am breaking it only to warn you of the bridge.
A shell on my hat for each shrine I have visited. Soon I shall need a larger hat.
The mist swallowed our guide on the forest road. We followed the sound of bells instead.
They say the water of the cathedral spring heals any wound. I have a thirst for miracles.
My husband is ill at home. I walk so that he may rise from his bed.
We pray at dawn, march at noon, and argue about directions every evening.
I gave my last coin to a leper on the road. That night I found two in my shoe.
Pilgrims are fed at the monastery gate. The soup is thin, but the welcome is warm.
Have you seen the great forges by night? We passed one and thought the world was ending.
Bless your blade, sister, at the next shrine you pass. Holy water never hurt good steel.
I collect pebbles from every holy place. My pack weighs more than my sins now.
The road is long, the road is hard, and the road is the only teacher I have ever obeyed.
I met a knight who walked his whole pilgrimage in full armour. He rusted at the first river.
At the last chapel, the candles lit themselves as we knelt. I swear it on my mother's soul.
Every step is a prayer, the friar says. Then I have prayed ten thousand times today.
We buried one of our band by the roadside. She was smiling. She had seen the shrine.
Watch for the stone markers with the carved star. They guide pilgrims through the wilds.
My feet are bleeding, my purse is empty, and my heart has never been lighter.
I left home to find paradise. So far I have found mostly turnips.
Walk with faith, sister. And with good boots, if faith runs short.
Spare a copper, lady? My belly has been singing hymns since yesterday.
I was a soldier once. Now I guard this doorway, for the price of a crust.
A coin for a secret? The guard captain sneaks into the tavern's back room every midnight.
Bless you, bless you! Or curse you, if you walk past. I am flexible.
Rich folk see right through me. I am a ghost who still needs bread.
Heard two merchants whisper about a chest buried under the old mill. Worth a coin, that is.
I sleep beside the bakery wall. The warm stones are the only kindness this city offers.
Look at you, all shiny armour. I had boots once. Good boots. Fond memories.
The rats here eat better than I do. I am thinking of joining them.
Nobody notices a beggar. That is why I hear everything worth hearing.
Your gold will not follow you into the grave, lady. But it could follow you into my cup.
The priests feed us on holy days. The rest of the week we are fed on promises.
Saw a hooded man drop something in the well last night. The water has tasted odd since.
I lost my leg to an orc's axe defending this city. The city lost my name the next day.
Alms for the poor! Alms for the wretched! Alms for the remarkably good looking!
One copper buys a bowl of soup. Two buys a bowl of soup with something floating in it.
The guards kick me off the steps each morning. I come back each noon. It is our little dance.
Got a crust? A rind? A kind word? I will take the word if it is all you have.
A noble's servant sold his master's silver to a man with a scarred lip. I know where he drinks.
I used to be a merchant. Then the mist took my caravan, and my luck, and my wife.
You go down below? Bring me back a spider leg. I hear they roast nicely.
Winter is coming and my blanket has more holes than cloth. Spare a little, lady?
Do not pity me. Pity the fat man who fears every thief. I sleep soundly.
The baker throws out yesterday's loaves at dusk. Do not tell the other beggars.
Heard tell the smith waters down his steel with tin. Check your blade twice, lady.
I am not drunk, lady. Hunger makes the world sway just the same.
Every coin you give is a prayer the saints actually hear. Mine, mostly.
My dog left me for a butcher's boy. Even dogs know where the meat is.
Someone has been digging in the graveyard by night. Not the gravedigger. He sleeps like the dead.
There is a door under the market that the watch pretends does not exist. Mind it, lady.
A copper, a crumb, or a curse. I accept all three, though I prefer the copper.
I begged at the lord's gate for twenty years. Then the mist came, and even the lords began begging.
Thank you kindly. Or I would thank you, had you given me anything.
Go well, lady, and come back rich. Generous too, if you can manage it.
Stand straight, sister. The undead smell fear the way hounds smell blood.
I swore my oath upon the sacred blade. It has not left my side in twenty winters.
The catacombs run deeper than any map shows. We guard every stair we know of.
Discipline before valour. A brave fool dies, a disciplined soldier returns.
Silver edge, blessed oil, and a steady arm. The restless dead fear nothing else.
Our order keeps vigil every night. One sleeping sentry is all the grave needs.
Wipe that blade clean after each fight. Corpse blood eats steel like rust.
I lost three brothers to a lich in the deep halls. I keep their names on my shield.
Do not pity the dead that walk. They are not the ones you buried. Strike without mercy.
The mist carries whispers that turn good men cowardly. Pray loud, and keep marching.
A templar sleeps in armour, eats standing, and prays kneeling. Rest is for the grave.
Fire and holy water. If a thing below survives both, run and warn us.
Courage is not the absence of fear. It is the oath that holds when fear does not.
Our grandmaster says the mist rises from a wound in the world. We mean to close it.
Keep your shield high and your faith higher. The daemons strike at both.
You fight well for one without an order. Have you thought of taking vows?
The bones of saints rest in our vaults. Anything that crawls toward them answers to my sword.
I have stood watch at the catacomb gate through nine winters. It has never once been quiet.
Mark the walls as you go below. A lost knight is a dead knight, and soon a walking one.
Ghouls are drawn to wounds. Bind every cut, no matter how small, before you rest.
Obey your orders, honour your oath, protect the weak. Everything else is noise.
I polish my armour each night. Not for vanity, sister. So the dead see me coming.
The skeletons in the deep still march in ranks. Someone down there drills them.
We hold the line so farmers can sleep. That is all the glory I need.
Never trust a necromancer's surrender. I learned that lesson with a scar.
Pray with me before you go below. Steel is stronger when the soul behind it is clean.
The bell above the chapter house rings when the dead stir. Last night it rang thrice.
Our order was founded in the ash of the first plague. We have never laid down arms since.
Speak no lies near the altar, sister. The saints are watching, and so am I.
When the torches gutter in the catacombs, close your eyes and listen. The dead never walk silently.
A sword is only iron. The oath is what gives it an edge.
Endure. That is the whole of the templar creed, written on a single line.
Should you fall below, we will come for your body before something else does.
Go with the saints' blessing, sister. Return with the dead behind you, never beside you.
What will it be, love? Ale, cider, or the stew that even the cook will not name?
Rooms are four silver a night, five if you want the bed without fleas.
Last night a dwarf drank three barrels and sang until the rafters wept. Then he paid in rubies.
Mind the drunk by the hearth. He swears he slew a dragon, and he swings when doubted.
Fresh barrel came in this morning. Brewed by monks, so it is practically holy.
A sailor swears the fog at sea has swallowed whole ships. I say he drank too much.
Wipe your boots, love. I just scrubbed that floor, and I will not scrub it twice for spider guts.
Every adventurer who walks through that door orders the strong stuff. I wonder why.
The mercenaries in the corner are celebrating. Of what, I do not want to know.
We had a brawl last week over a game of knucklebones. The table lost.
If you hear screaming upstairs, it is only the bard practising. Mostly.
Rumour has it the forge masters are buying every scrap of iron in the land.
My ale is cheap, my wine is cheaper, and my advice is free. Stay out of the mist.
Pay up front, love. Too many guests go below and never come back to settle their tab.
Hot bath out back, a copper a bucket. You look like you need several buckets.
That cloaked fellow has nursed one cup all evening. Quiet ones are either broke or trouble.
The cook's pie is famous across three valleys. Nobody can agree whether famous is the right word.
Mind the stairs on your way up. The third step bites, and I have not had it fixed.
Two farmers came in yesterday swearing they saw a troll on the north road. I gave them a stronger ale.
The bard owes me two weeks' board. If he plays that one song again, I am taking it in lute strings.
Here's to you, love. May your purse be heavy and your enemies light.
Lost and found is behind the bar. Mostly teeth, but there is a good dagger in there.
My grandfather built this place with his own hands. He also built the leaning wall. Do not lean on it.
A pilgrim, a templar and a thief walked in last night. Only the thief tipped.
Keep your hand on your purse, love. The pretty ones at the dice table are quick fingered.
Kitchen closes at midnight, bar closes at dawn, and the snoring never closes at all.
A boatman swore the drowned walk the sewers by night. Then he ordered a fish supper.
Spilled ale, broken chairs, a bard in the rain barrel. A quiet night, all told.
You are welcome here any time, love. Coin always is.
The mage who rented the attic left a smell like burnt lightning. I have been airing it out for days.
I water the ale on feast days. Do not tell anyone, or I will water yours too.
Sit by the fire and dry those boots. The stew will be along shortly, unless the cat finds it first.
I have heard every tale under the sun in this tavern. Yours had better be a good one.
Drink up, love. Tomorrow the dungeon, tonight the ale.
